subject: AI & Agents
title: Backpropagation: The Algorithm That Changed Everything
description: A short lesson to help you apply Backpropagation: The Algorithm That Changed Everything.

hook.text: In 1986, a paper showed how to teach multi-layer neural networks. The perceptron's curse was broken.

buildup.text: Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams popularized backpropagation — learning by correcting errors backward.

discovery.text: Each layer adjusts its weights based on how much it contributed to the final error.

twist.text: The idea had been discovered multiple times before, but this time computers were powerful enough.

climax.text: Backpropagation unlocked deep networks. Without it, modern AI wouldn't exist.

punchline.text: Learn from mistakes, layer by layer.

quiz.question: What does backpropagation do?
options: Adjusts neural network weights by propagating errors backward

details.summary: Backpropagation, popularized by Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams in 1986, enables neural networks to learn by propagating errors backward. It is the algorithm that makes training deep networks possible.
details.whyItMatters: Without backpropagation, neural networks would be unable to learn efficiently. This single algorithm underpins virtually all deep learning, making it arguably the most important algorithm in AI history.
takeaways: Backpropagation calculates how to adjust each network weight
It propagates error signals backward through the network layers
Nearly all modern deep learning depends on this algorithm

faq.question: How does backpropagation work in simple terms?
faq.answer: After the network makes a prediction, the error is calculated. Backpropagation traces how much each weight contributed to the error. Each weight is then adjusted proportionally to reduce the error next time.

faq.question: Why was backpropagation not widely used until the 1980s?
faq.answer: The basic idea existed earlier, but Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams demonstrated it could train multi-layer networks effectively. Earlier computing hardware was also too slow to make it practical.
